title: Risk Assessment: Scope agent prompts to role-relevant context only
summary: Assessment of the proposed _build_role_context() helper approach (Approach A) for replacing the one-size-fits-all pipeline.prompt embedding with role-appropriate context. This change modifies the prompt construction pipeline in a single file (orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py) and its test file. The overall risk is Low-Medium: the change is well-scoped (pure prompt content changes, no schema or data model modifications), but carries regression risk from modifying a 300-line function that affects all agent types. Six risks identified: three Medium, three Low. All are mitigable with the recommended phased approach and test-first strategy.

risk_assessment.overall_verdict: Proceed with Approach A (_build_role_context() helper). Risks are manageable with the two-phase implementation plan. The change is purely additive in terms of code structure (new helper functions) and subtractive in terms of prompt content (less context per role). No schema changes, no data model changes, no new dependencies. The primary risk is behavioral regression — agents receiving less context than they need — which is mitigated by the 'summarize, don't omit' principle and 'For more context' pointers.
risk_assessment.confidence: High — based on source code analysis of _build_agent_prompt() (lines 1942-2240), _build_phase_scoped_prompt() (lines 2243-2348), _run_tier3_implement() (lines 2351-3033), _run_multi_agent_phase() (lines 3062-3149), existing test patterns in test_pipeline_prompts.py and test_tier3_dispatch.py, and the plan template format (docs/templates/plan.md)

risks.title: Scoped agents lack sufficient context and produce worse outputs
risks.description: The core risk of this change: agents that currently see the full issue body will instead see a 1-2 sentence summary. If the summary omits information that an agent needs to make good decisions — e.g., edge cases mentioned in the issue that a tester should verify, or constraints mentioned in the issue that a documenter should reflect — agent output quality could degrade. This is especially concerning for testers in Tier 3 where phase context is narrow and the tester relies on understanding the broader intent to design meaningful tests. The issue explicitly warns about this: 'Focus, Don't Starve — an agent that lacks orientation will make poor decisions or spin trying to figure out its purpose.'

mitigation.strategy: Comprehensive 'For more context' pointers + quality-preserving summaries
steps: Every scoped prompt MUST include 'For more context: gh issue view <N>' and relevant file paths — agents can self-serve additional context on demand
The _summarize_issue() helper should use issue title + first paragraph (not just title) to preserve key context
For tester prompts: include acceptance criteria verbatim (not summarized) since these are the testing contract
For documenter prompts: include task descriptions that explain what was built, not just file lists
Run a manual smoke test comparing old vs new prompts for at least one recent Tier 3 pipeline to verify sufficient context
Monitor first 2-3 pipelines after deployment for signs of agent confusion or task spinning
mitigation.residual_risk: Low — agents can access full context via CLI commands, and the summary preserves orientation. The issue explicitly says a few hundred extra tokens is fine.

risks.review_reason: Human should review sample scoped prompts for tester and documenter roles to verify they contain sufficient context for good agent performance. Compare against the current full-issue-body prompts.

risks.title: Plan filtering in _build_phase_scoped_prompt() breaks on non-standard plan formats
risks.description: The proposed change to _build_phase_scoped_prompt() requires parsing the plan draft to extract the overview section and filter to the current phase. The architect proposes heading-level parsing ('## for sections, ### for phases'). While the plan template (docs/templates/plan.md) defines a standard format ('## Summary', '### Phase N: [Name]'), existing plan drafts may vary — e.g., using '## Implementation Phases' vs '## Phases', or having additional sections between the summary and phases. The plan is generated by AI agents which may deviate from the template. If parsing fails, the fallback (embedding the full plan) preserves current behavior but defeats the purpose. A partial parse that silently drops content is worse — it could omit the current phase's tasks.

mitigation.strategy: Defensive parsing with full-plan fallback and validation
steps: Implement plan parsing with explicit fallback: if current phase heading is not found, embed the full plan with a log warning rather than silently dropping content
Match phase headings flexibly: look for '### Phase N' patterns with regex, not exact string matching, to handle minor template variations
Extract everything before the first '### Phase' heading as the 'overview' section (catches '## Summary', '## Implementation Phases', or whatever comes first)
Add unit tests with at least 3 plan formats: (a) standard template, (b) plan with extra sections, (c) plan where current phase heading is missing — verify fallback triggers
Sample 3-5 existing plan drafts from .egg-state/drafts/ to verify the parser handles real-world formats
mitigation.residual_risk: Low — full-plan fallback preserves current behavior. Partial parses are the only danger, and validation prevents those.

risks.title: _build_agent_prompt() signature change breaks call sites or tests
risks.description: The architect recommends adding a 'pipeline: Pipeline | None = None' optional parameter to _build_agent_prompt() to pass the Pipeline object for role-context building. There are 4 call sites in pipelines.py (lines 2555, 2631, 2961, 3108) plus the test file test_tier3_dispatch.py (which imports and calls _build_phase_scoped_prompt). All call sites use keyword arguments. Adding an optional parameter with a default of None is backward-compatible. However, the _build_role_context() function needs the Pipeline object to access issue_number and issue title for the summary. If a call site passes prompt=pipeline.prompt but not pipeline=pipeline, _build_role_context() would lack the data to build a summary, and must fall back to the raw prompt. This creates two code paths: one with Pipeline (uses role context) and one without (falls back to current behavior). Both paths must be tested.

mitigation.strategy: Update all 4 call sites atomically and add the pipeline parameter with backward-compatible default
steps: Add pipeline: Pipeline | None = None as an optional parameter with default None
In _build_agent_prompt(), when pipeline is provided, use _build_role_context() for context. When pipeline is None, fall back to existing 'if prompt:' behavior
Update all 4 call sites to pass pipeline=pipeline alongside the existing prompt=pipeline.prompt
The prompt parameter can remain for backward compatibility — _build_role_context() uses the Pipeline object preferentially
Add tests for both code paths: with pipeline object (new behavior) and without (backward-compatible fallback)
Run existing tests to verify no regressions before adding new functionality
mitigation.residual_risk: Very Low — adding an optional parameter with a default is inherently backward-compatible. All call sites have the Pipeline object available.

risks.title: No existing tests for _build_agent_prompt() role-specific content — regressions may go undetected
risks.description: The architect's analysis correctly identifies that test_pipeline_prompts.py (738 lines, 12 test classes) has NO tests for _build_agent_prompt() role-specific context. Tests exist for _build_phase_scoped_prompt() in test_tier3_dispatch.py (TestPhaseScopedPrompt class), but these test the phase-scoped coder prompt, not the tester/documenter/integrator prompts. This means the current prompt content for these roles is effectively untested — both the existing behavior and the proposed changes lack a test safety net. If the refactor introduces a bug in, say, the integrator prompt, no test would catch it.

mitigation.strategy: Write tests before modifying code — test-first approach
steps: Phase 1 should START by adding tests for the current _build_agent_prompt() behavior for tester, documenter, and integrator roles — this establishes a baseline
These baseline tests should assert that the current prompts contain '## Task Description' and the prompt content — they will intentionally break when the refactor changes behavior
After the refactor, update the baseline tests to assert the new behavior: summary present, full issue body absent (for scoped roles), 'For more context' pointers present
Add dedicated TestBuildRoleContext and TestSummarizeIssue test classes that test the new helpers in isolation
For plan filtering: add tests using mock plan content with known heading structure
mitigation.residual_risk: Low — test-first approach ensures both old and new behavior are verified

risks.title: _summarize_issue() produces poor summaries for edge-case issue formats
risks.description: The proposed _summarize_issue(title, body) helper extracts a 1-2 sentence summary from the issue title + first paragraph, truncated at ~200 chars at a sentence boundary. Edge cases: (1) issue body starts with a heading ('## Problem') rather than a paragraph — the first 'paragraph' may be just a heading with no content, (2) issue body uses bullet points instead of paragraphs — the first 'paragraph' may be a single bullet, (3) issue body is very short or empty — the summary is just the title, (4) issue title is very long (>100 chars) — combined with a paragraph, the summary exceeds the expected token budget. These are all handled gracefully by the 'summarize, don't omit' philosophy — even a mediocre summary plus the full issue pointer is better than a multi-thousand-token issue body.

mitigation.strategy: Simple implementation with generous limits and explicit edge case handling
steps: Use issue title as the primary summary sentence — it's always present and descriptive
For the body, strip markdown headings (lines starting with #) and extract the first non-empty paragraph (split by blank lines)
If no suitable paragraph is found, use just the title — this is acceptable per the issue's guidelines
Set a generous character limit (~300 chars, not strict 200) to avoid cutting mid-concept
Unit test with: normal issue, heading-first issue, bullet-list issue, empty body, very long title
mitigation.residual_risk: Very Low — the worst case is a slightly suboptimal summary, which is still far better than the full issue body

risks.title: Changes to _build_agent_prompt() inadvertently affect plan-phase agents (architect, task_planner, risk_analyst)
risks.description: The issue explicitly states that architect, task_planner, and risk_analyst should continue receiving the full issue body. However, all roles flow through the same _build_agent_prompt() function. If the refactored code has a bug in the role-dispatch logic — e.g., using _build_role_context() for all roles and the role check has a typo — plan-phase agents could lose the full issue body and receive only a summary. This would cripple the quality of analysis, plan, and risk outputs. The current 'if prompt:' block is role-agnostic (it embeds the prompt for everyone), so there's no existing code path that demonstrates correct role-based filtering.

mitigation.strategy: Explicit allowlist for full-context roles + dedicated test
steps: In _build_role_context(), use an explicit allowlist constant: FULL_CONTEXT_ROLES = {'architect', 'task_planner', 'risk_analyst'}
The default behavior should be the new scoped context — only roles in the allowlist get the full body. This is fail-safe: new roles get scoped context, not full
Add a test that explicitly verifies each allowlisted role receives pipeline.prompt verbatim in the output
Add a test that explicitly verifies tester, documenter, and integrator do NOT receive pipeline.prompt verbatim
mitigation.residual_risk: Very Low — explicit allowlist with dedicated tests prevents accidental exclusion

areas_requiring_human_review.reason: R-1 — Human should review the actual prompt output for tester and documenter roles with the new _build_role_context() to verify agents receive sufficient context. This is a judgment call that cannot be fully automated.

rollback_plan.strategy: Feature flag via role-context dispatch, or simple revert
rollback_plan.details: The change is contained within a single file (orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py) and its test files. Rollback options: (1) Revert the commits — since the change is purely prompt content, no data migration or schema change is needed. (2) Add a flag in _build_role_context() that returns pipeline.prompt for all roles regardless of role (effectively disabling scoping). Option 1 is preferred since this is a clean refactor with no persistent state changes.
steps: If agents show degraded behavior after deployment, revert the PR (git revert)
No data migration needed — prompt content changes are stateless
No downstream consumer changes — handoff data mechanism is untouched
If only one role is affected, targeted fix: change _build_role_context() to return full prompt for that specific role

implementation_recommendations.rationale: No tests exist for the current behavior of _build_agent_prompt() for non-coder roles. Adding baseline tests first ensures we can detect regressions and validates our understanding of the current behavior.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Use an explicit FULL_CONTEXT_ROLES allowlist constant
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Prevents accidental exclusion of plan-phase agents from the full issue body. A constant is easy to audit and update.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Implement plan filtering with a full-plan fallback, not a silent partial parse
implementation_recommendations.rationale: If the plan heading parser cannot find the current phase, embedding the full plan (current behavior) is safe. Silently dropping content is the danger.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Verify plan parsing against 3-5 real plan drafts from .egg-state/drafts/
implementation_recommendations.rationale: The .egg-state/drafts/ directory contains dozens of real plan files generated by prior pipelines. Testing the parser against these ensures it handles real-world format variation.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Keep the prompt parameter in _build_agent_prompt() for backward compatibility
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Adding pipeline as a parallel optional parameter avoids breaking any code paths that don't have a Pipeline object. The function should prefer pipeline when available and fall back to the raw prompt otherwise.

phase_1.name: Core helper functions and _build_agent_prompt refactor
phase_1.rationale: This phase modifies the _build_agent_prompt() function that affects ALL non-coder agent prompts. A bug here impacts every role. However, the change is well-defined: replace a 4-line unconditional block with a role-dispatched helper. The backward-compatible fallback (when pipeline param is not provided) limits blast radius.

phase_2.name: Phase-scoped plan filtering and integration tests
phase_2.rationale: This phase modifies _build_phase_scoped_prompt() which only affects Tier 3 coders. The change is isolated: replace full plan embedding with filtered content. The full-plan fallback preserves current behavior if parsing fails. Only one function is modified.

compatibility_assessment.schema_changes: None — no model or data schema changes
compatibility_assessment.breaking_changes: None — the change is internal to prompt construction

security_assessment.details: This change only affects the text content of agent prompts. It does not modify: authentication, authorization, file access controls, gateway enforcement, or any security boundary. The prompt content is generated server-side from trusted sources (Pipeline model fields). No user input is processed differently.
